_doc: Headwaters source registry - PLATFORM-SCOPE families (P5-6). Datasets used by every city, registered once here instead of duplicated per city. Only families that actually VERSION belong here: OpenStreetMap and Google Dynamic World are continuously updated with no editions, so they stay in the coverage allowlist as a freshness question (P5-1), not an edition watch. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). CADENCE + TIER ARE DOCUMENTATION ONLY - decided 2026-07-26. Neither gates polling: every non-ciBlocked entry is fetched on every weekly run whatever its declared cadence (48 HTTP requests per CI run across ~26 hosts). Deliberate. (1) Cadence is a CLAIM and claims are wrong - CPCB is 'yearly' and shipped a mid-year Yamuna-only file, BBMB was recorded frozen and had resumed, CHIRPS looked daily and publishes monthly; gating polls on a declared cadence inherits every such error and stops looking at exactly the source that surprised you. (2) A conditional check is a check that can silently stop - the WRIS 'green for 39 days while ingesting nothing' bug lives in skip logic. (3) Interval scheduling is maintenance overhead for no real saving at this volume. Cadence earns its place at REVIEW time instead: it tells you whether a detection is plausible - a 'yearly' source producing a new edition three weeks after the last is itself a signal.

sources.notes: FABDEM V1-2 - satellite DEM with buildings and forests removed - underpins the elevation-band layer in all five cities, honest at ~30 m horizontal / ~2 m vertical. A new FABDEM version changes every band boundary at once, which is exactly why this is registered once at platform scope rather than five times. LICENCE FLAG: FABDEM is CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial - relevant if any BRSR or commercial track ever reuses these layers. The canonical data host is data.bris.ac.uk but its dataset paths need an exact opaque id we do not have; the Fathom product page is the stable, verified surface (200 on 2026-07-26). Cascade catchment delineation (catchments_fabdem_wbt_v1 in neer-vazhvu-api/app/cascade/catchments.py) runs on a FABDEM mosaic, so the entire public/data/cascade family is FABDEM-DERIVED - and therefore inherits CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial) encumbrance. Flagged for the NVDM derivative-licence audit 2026-07-30. LICENCE: confirmed at data.bris.ac.uk/data/dataset/s5hqmjcdj8yo2ibzi9b4ew3sn (verified 2026-07-31): 'The FABDEM dataset is licensed under a Creative Commons "CC BY-NC-SA 4.0" license. For commercial use queries, please contact fabdem@fathom.global'. ShareAlike is the sharp edge, not just NC: anything built on FABDEM must be redistributed under the same licence, which is why the repo MIT LICENSE cannot reach the cascade artefacts.

sources.license: HydroSHEDS v1 bespoke WWF licence, not an open licence: the technical documentation s.7.1 states the core data are 'free for non-commercial and commercial use', but Appendix A s.2.1.2 bars distributing the Licensed Materials 'as a stand-alone product', s.2.2 makes the Exhibit B attribution mandatory (reproduced in DATA-LICENSE.md), and s.3 asserts that WWF 'shall own and retain all Intellectual Property Rights in the Licensed Materials and any modifications, extensions, or improvements of the Licensed Materials however developed'
sources.notes: HydroBASINS/HydroRIVERS is the skeleton under every cascade reconstruction (Chennai 755 nodes, Bengaluru 1,033, plus Madurai and Mumbai) and under the Chennai sub-basin climate-risk clip (hybas_12 + state clip). A version bump would move cascade topology everywhere at once - a platform-wide SCHEMA-BREAK candidate, not a routine roll-forward. page-hash may be noisy on a marketing-styled page; tighten with a selector if it false-positives. LICENCE: all four clauses read from the HydroSHEDS v1.4 Technical Documentation PDF (verified 2026-07-31). The previous string, 'free for non-commercial and most uses', was wrong in both directions: it invented a commercial bar that the licence does not contain, and omitted the stand-alone-distribution bar, the mandatory Exhibit B attribution and the s.3 ownership claim over modifications - which on its face reaches catchment topology derived here. Still classified non-commercial by scripts/nvdm-encumbrance-report.py, deliberately: a bespoke contract with an ownership claim over our own derivatives is not a clean source, and the audit fails closed.

sources.license: Copernicus free and open data, attribution required; GSW download page states 'All data here is produced under the Copernicus Programme and is provided free of charge, without restriction of use', required attribution 'Source: EC JRC/Google' plus Pekel et al. sources.notes: JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 supplies the long-run water-extent trend in every rich-body deep-zoom panel across the 20-body cohort. A new JRC version re-bases those trends, so it is a review event rather than an auto-apply. dependsOn points at the rich-bodies GROUP - the coverage gate collapses that directory to one logical artifact rather than 129 folders.

Google Open Buildings v3 is one of the two independent building-footprint sources in the rich-body encroachment verification; Overture is the other, and the artifacts deliberately compare them side by side. A version bump on either changes the verification result, which is why both are registered.

Overture ships MONTHLY, the fastest cadence of any platform family, and a workflow already re-pulls it on the 8th - so this entry is about knowing the release landed, not about triggering the fetch. GAP FOUND 2026-07-26: our overture artifacts record only computed_at, NOT the Overture release version they were built from, so we cannot currently tell which release a given rich-body panel reflects. Worth adding to the ingest script. docs.overturemaps.org/release/ 404s and the GitHub releases API returns an empty list, so overturemaps.org/download is the watchable surface.

sources.notes: MOVED to platform scope 2026-07-31 (#220 review): a national CPCB report whose dependsOn spans Bangalore, the Arkavathi basin pack, and the Mumbai facts register - a city-scope entry misfiled cross-city lineage. Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality - the BOD-band Priority I-V classification behind the Arkavathi atlas, the Bengaluru stretch classes, the Chennai Cooum/Adyar Priority I status and the Mumbai 'Mithi at Mahim is India's worst stretch' fact. WHY page-hash and not link-set: the landing page exposes no report hrefs at all - only CPCB's site-wide boilerplate PDFs (verified 2026-07-26) - and the report itself was published behind an openpdffile.php id that has since expired (it now returns a 146-byte HTML error mislabelled application/pdf). Expect page-hash to be noisier than link-set; tighten with a selector if it false-positives. Host note: cpcb.gov.in, never the NICNET cpcb DOT nic DOT in - see cpcb-nwmp-annual. LICENCE: read from cpcb.gov.in/copyright-policy/ (verified 2026-07-31). The previous 'GoI publication, cited with attribution' was wrong: CPCB does not use the liberal GIGW template, it uses the permission-required one. Extracted factual values are a separate question (no copyright in facts), but the reports themselves are not redistributable and the artefacts are no longer licence-clean. MIRROR REMOVED 2026-07-31: public/docs/cpcb-polluted-river-stretches-oct-2025.pdf (4.4 MB) was a redistributed copy of a report whose publisher requires approval for any use beyond download and print. Deleted; all citations now point at https://cpcb.gov.in/polluted-river-stretches/. The extracted BOD-band values stay - facts carry no copyright - only the document itself is gone. Operators refreshing this source fetch the PDF locally and must not commit it; scripts/check-mirrored-documents.py enforces that.
